review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner, self-review of the rereview regression design
review.decision: Keep same-thread recovery under the publication lease, retain positive retirement/exit proof at relocated aliases, and isolate independent historical fixtures.
review.notes: Based on the user's direct independent review of ce9d4a2b / bcd7d82f and official failing run 44870380228. The GitHub Go failure was in restore fixture setup. All tests use isolated roots and do not touch current processes or production metadata.

cases.description: An older same-thread index is repaired under a continuous publication lease
cases.setup: Actual heartbeat and a legacy same-thread index with an intact exact private receipt; inject a competing Save during strict re-observation.
cases.action: Attempt the competing write in the historical release/reacquire window, and separately model a visible old-binary update before the final comparison.
cases.expected: An upgraded writer receives contention or proves its write occurs before or after repair. A visible changed version survives. A serialized successful repair retains same-thread historical fields.

cases.description: Normal closure retires all exact moved aliases, retaining evidence on metadata write failure
cases.setup: Real verified frontend across multiple relocations, and a closure with injected private index write failure.
cases.action: Close the original bridge while testing legacy admission and live reads in the current and old locations.
cases.expected: Committed aliases explicitly release without becoming live. The error path preserves an exact closed receipt rather than deleting the only process witness; it never grants live input and permits subsequent legitimate publication.

cases.description: Older receipt unlink requires positive exact native terminal exit proof
cases.setup: Legacy managed index without frontend receipt, with an independent exact native binding record or identity-mismatched control.
cases.action: Try publication with an alive or unknown foreground PID, then prove the exact recorded terminal process is gone.
cases.expected: Absent, unreadable, unrelated or alive proof cannot release. A matching private native receipt with positive process absence can release the legacy index without granting live authority.

cases.description: Same and foreign home restore checks start from independently captured history
cases.setup: Existing saved Codex restore subtests use independent location keys and retain their original home, launcher, link and expected authority.
cases.action: Seed each history independently and run the actual restore eligibility and live ownership checks.
cases.expected: Fixture setup never asks the stricter publisher to overwrite an unrelated previous case's managed index. All original restore and home-scope assertions remain unchanged.
